feedback.finish: Roman soldiers were well-equipped and well-trained. This is one of the main reasons why they were so successful in expanding their empire.

atoms.text: As the Roman army conquered new territories, they built long, straight roads to connect the empire. This allowed soldiers, supplies and messengers to travel faster from place to place.

Approximately every four miles, there were stables, where soldiers and other officials could switch horses. Rome also maintained stopping places called mansiones every twelve miles. Roman officials could rest here and stay overnight while travelling.
atoms.sound: Approximately every four miles, there were stables, where soldiers and other officials could switch horses. Rome also maintained stopping places called mahn-siones every twelve miles. Roman officials could rest here and stay overnight while travelling.

atoms.a: Most people in the Roman army were legionaries. These were highly-disciplined, professional foot soldiers that fought in units of around 5,000 men known as legions.
Each legion had a special standard bearer, who carried a pole with a golden eagle into battle. Losing this eagle was considered to be a deep disgrace for the legion!
A centurion was in charge of a smaller unit of around 80 soldiers known as a century. They were distinguished by their sideways helmet plume.

hint.text: The Romans often wrote letters on thin pieces of wood, called tabellae, which were an everyday way to send messages before paper became common.

atoms.finishSound: Soldiers had to serve in the army for 25 years.
The pay soldiers received was steady.

instruction.text: Read and select the correct answers.

atoms.text: The Romans also recruited new soldiers from the areas they conquered. While these soldiers were paid less than the Roman soldiers, they could earn citizenship after their 25 years of service.

Many men across the empire took up this offer, with around half of the army being made up of such people! These non-citizen soldiers, or auxiliaries, could not fight in a legion and instead formed more specialised units of archers, scouts and cavalry.
